title: Aamir Khan Is Going Back to Cricket. This Time the Story Is Real, Set During Partition, and Involves the Man Who Scored India's First Test Century.
excerpt: Twenty-five years after Lagaan earned an Oscar nomination, Aamir Khan and Ashutosh Gowariker are reuniting for a biopic of Lala Amarnath — India's fearless first cricket captain whose friendship with Pakistan's Abdul Hafeez Kardar survived the bloodiest chapter in subcontinental history.
body:
The last time Aamir Khan and Ashutosh Gowariker made a cricket film together, it ended up at the Oscars. That was Lagaan, released in 2001, about a fictional village and a fictional match against fictional colonizers. Their next collaboration is none of those things.

The two are reuniting for an untitled biopic of Lala Amarnath, India's first Test centurion and first captain of independent India. The film is expected to center on the historic 1952 India-Pakistan Test series and the extraordinary friendship between Amarnath and Pakistan captain Abdul Hafeez Kardar — two men who grew up together in Lahore, were torn apart by Partition, and met again on a cricket field that carried the weight of two new nations.

Shooting is scheduled to begin in October 2026.

## Why This Story Matters Now

Lala Amarnath Bhardwaj was born in 1911 in Kapurthala, Punjab, and became the first Indian to score a Test century — 118 against England at Bombay's Gymkhana Ground in 1933. He was 22 years old. The innings was equal parts talent and defiance; he was famously fearless, combative with authority, and uninterested in the deference that British cricket expected from Indian players.

But the film isn't about that century. According to reports, the screenplay — developed with creative input from Rajkumar Hirani and writer Abhijat Joshi — focuses on the 1952 series, the first Test contest between India and Pakistan after Partition. Amarnath captained India to a 2-1 series victory. More significant than the result was the context: barely five years after Partition had killed between one and two million people, two cricket teams stood on the same field and played a game that millions on both sides desperately wanted to mean something.

## The Partition Angle and the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, Partition is not ancient history. It is the reason many families ended up where they are. The trauma, the displacement, the stories passed down across generations of relatives who fled Lahore or Rawalpindi or Dhaka — these are living memories in millions of NRI households.

A Bollywood film that addresses Partition through sport rather than through violence is a rare thing. The 2021 film 83, which depicted India's 1983 World Cup win, proved that cricket stories have massive diaspora appeal. But 83 was a triumph narrative. This film is attempting something harder: a story about two friends on opposite sides of a wound that hasn't fully healed, trying to hold onto their humanity through a game.

Aamir Khan's involvement elevates the stakes. He hasn't delivered a commercial hit since Dangal in 2016. Thugs of Hindostan (2018), Laal Singh Chaddha (2022), and Sitaare Zameen Par (2024) all underperformed. But he remains one of the few Indian actors whose films are treated as cultural events rather than opening-weekend products. A period cricket drama set during Partition, made by the Lagaan team, with Hirani's fingerprints on the script — this is the kind of project that could either redeem his decade-long slump or become the most expensive misfire of his career.

## Three Films in the Pipeline

The Lala Amarnath biopic is the first in a three-film plan that represents the most productive stretch of Aamir Khan's late career. After the biopic wraps, he is expected to begin work on Rajkumar Hirani's sequel to 3 Idiots, now pushed to a mid-2027 floor. Reports suggest the sequel will feature a significant time jump and potentially reunite the original trio of Aamir Khan, R. Madhavan, and Sharman Joshi, with Vicky Kaushal joining the cast in a new role.

The production timeline is aggressive by Aamir's standards. He has historically taken two to three years between films, spending months on physical preparation and script refinement. Committing to shoot the biopic from October 2026 and then pivot to the 3 Idiots sequel by mid-2027 suggests a sense of urgency — or at least an awareness that at 61, the window for physically demanding roles is narrowing.

## Gowariker's Redemption Arc

For Ashutosh Gowariker, the reunion is equally significant. After Lagaan, his career produced exactly one critical and commercial hit — Jodhaa Akbar (2008). Everything else — Swades (cult following, box office failure), What's Your Raashee?, Mohenjo Daro, Panipat — either flopped or was ignored. He is among the most respected and least commercially successful directors in Hindi cinema.

A return to cricket, with Aamir, on a story that combines the two subjects Gowariker handles best (history and sport) feels like a filmmaker getting one more shot at the thing he was always meant to make. The pressure will be immense. The Lagaan comparison will be unavoidable. But if the 1952 series provides the same kind of emotionally specific, culturally loaded narrative that Champaner did, the comparison might be the point.

## What to Watch For

The production will face challenges that Lagaan never did. Period accuracy for 1950s India-Pakistan relations will require navigating political sensitivities that have only intensified in recent years. Casting the Pakistani team — particularly Kardar — will be scrutinized on both sides of the border. And the cricket sequences will need to match the technical bar set by 83, which raised the standard for sports filmmaking in India.

But the bones of the story are extraordinary. A man who fled a mob in Lahore during Partition, who used a cricket match to extend diplomacy that politicians couldn't, who treated his opponents with warmth when hatred would have been easier. In a film landscape increasingly dominated by franchise sequels and action spectacles, that's a story worth telling.

October 2026. Aamir Khan will shave his head, or grow a mustache, or gain thirty pounds. He'll do whatever he always does. And then we'll see if Champaner was lightning in a bottle, or the beginning of something that still has a chapter left.
